items.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I’d love to be able to play with somebody like Milt Jackson because he’s one of the few outstanding guys I can think of that can lead a quartet.

ctx.x: If you could write your own ticket for the next three or four years — play with anybody, go anywhere, do anything, your dream requisition — what would be on it?

Well like I told Mike LeDonne, I’d like to play with Milt Jackson. There’s so few guys around, well you know like I said I liked Sonny Rollins the way he used to play back 30 years ago. And I still like him, he’s a wonderful guy, it’s just that he’s so far out. But I mean anyhow, I would like to play with, you know like I say I’m old enough that I started with the old even Dixieland you know I played with a lot of Dixieland bands too. And I don’t put any of that down. But I just happened to, my favorite is sort…
Well thank you very much for conversing with us. Mary do you have another question you might ask?
